text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government names 172-man panel of prominent traditional rulers, serving and former ministers, captains of industries, media executives and others to chart "Vision 2010" economic development programme
- Government to announce soon new package of incentives for oil producing companies in Nigeria, official sources say.
- Some 35,000 metric tonnes of rice are expected at Tin Can Island port in Lagos by mid-December, according to shipping manifest at the port.
- Six billion naira will be spent to curb erosion of Lagos beach, says Works Minister Major-General Abdulkareem Adisa.
- European Union extends for another six months sanctions imposed on Nigeria in the wake of annulment of 1993 presidential vote and hanging of nine minority rights activists.
- Seventeen Nigerians died while four others survived the Ethiopian plane crash in the Indian Ocean at the weekend.
- Afprint Nigeria Plc plans to set up a one billion naira oil mill to process 300 metric tonnes of cotton seed daily in northern city of Zaria, says executive director Ajit Mishra.
- Canadian experts commence computerisation of Nigerian stock exchange.
- Agricultural credit officers of the central bank at three-day workshop recommend establishment without delay of a Nigerian commodity exchange.
